# Gentleskin

> A gentle iPhone app for tracking skin picking (dermatillomania, excoriation disorder) and other body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs). Log a pick in two taps, see patterns, ride out urges, and make a PDF report for a therapist.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6789245158
- Price: 7-day free trial, then $29.99/year or $5.99/month (US; varies by region)

## Guides

- [What is dermatillomania (skin picking disorder)? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/what-is-dermatillomania/): Dermatillomania, also called excoriation disorder, is repeated skin picking that a person can't stop and that damages the skin. How it's diagnosed and where to find help.
- [What are BFRBs (body-focused repetitive behaviors)? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/bfrbs/): BFRBs are a family of repetitive behaviors like skin picking, hair pulling and nail biting that damage the body and are hard to stop.
- [Is skin picking self-harm? Is it vanity? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/is-skin-picking-self-harm/): Skin picking isn't self-harm and isn't vanity. What drives it, according to the TLC Foundation, the NHS and the MSD Manual.
- [Focused vs automatic skin picking | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/focused-vs-automatic-picking/): Researchers describe two kinds of skin picking: focused (on purpose, often at a mirror) and automatic (without noticing). Why the difference changes what helps.
- [Treatment for skin picking: what has evidence | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/skin-picking-treatment/): The treatments for skin picking disorder with the most evidence: habit reversal training and CBT. What happens in them, and where medication fits.
- [Why do I pick my skin? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/why-do-i-pick-my-skin/): Why people pick their skin: stress relief, boredom, the feel of a bump, the mirror, tiredness. Automatic and focused picking, and why it's so hard to stop.
- [How to find help for skin picking | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/find-help-for-skin-picking/): Where to find a therapist who treats skin picking: the TLC Foundation and IOCDF directories, your doctor, and the NHS in the UK.
- [Talking to family and friends about skin picking | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/talking-to-family-about-skin-picking/): How to tell family or friends about skin picking, and what to ask them to do (and not do).
- [How to stop picking your skin | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/how-to-stop-picking-skin/): How habit reversal training works for skin picking: noticing when you pick, changing your surroundings, giving your hands something else to do, and waiting out urges.
- [CBT for skin picking: what happens in therapy | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/cbt-for-skin-picking/): How cognitive behavioral therapy treats skin picking: habit reversal, the ComB model, working with the thoughts that give you permission to pick, and how to find a therapist.
- [Urge surfing for skin picking | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/urge-surfing/): Urge surfing is a way to wait out the urge to pick your skin by watching it rise and fall instead of acting on it. How to do it.
- [Scalp picking: why it happens and how to cut down | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/scalp-picking/): Scalp picking is a common form of skin picking. Why people pick at the scalp, and what helps them cut down.
- [Tracking skin picking, and what to bring to therapy | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/guides/tracking-skin-picking/): Why tracking skin picking helps, what to write down, and what to show a therapist.

## Guías en español

- [¿Qué es la dermatilomanía (trastorno por excoriación)? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/que-es-la-dermatilomania/): La dermatilomanía, o trastorno por excoriación, es pellizcarse la piel una y otra vez sin poder parar, al punto de dañarla. Cómo se diagnostica y dónde buscar ayuda.
- [¿Qué son los BFRB (conductas repetitivas centradas en el cuerpo)? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/bfrb/): Los BFRB son una familia de conductas como pellizcarse la piel, arrancarse el pelo o morderse las uñas, que dañan el cuerpo y cuestan mucho dejar.
- [¿Pellizcarse la piel es autolesión? ¿Es vanidad? | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/no-es-vanidad-ni-autolesion/): La dermatilomanía no es autolesión ni vanidad. Qué hay detrás, según la TLC Foundation, el NHS y el Manual MSD.
- [Pellizcarse concentrado o en automático | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/pellizcar-concentrado-o-automatico/): Los investigadores describen dos formas de pellizcarse la piel: concentrada (a propósito, a menudo frente al espejo) y automática (sin darte cuenta). Por qué cambia lo que ayuda.
- [Tratamiento de la dermatilomanía: qué tiene evidencia | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/tratamiento/): Los tratamientos con más evidencia para la dermatilomanía: inversión del hábito y terapia cognitivo-conductual. En qué consisten y dónde entra la medicación.
- [Dónde buscar ayuda para la dermatilomanía | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/donde-buscar-ayuda/): Dónde encontrar un terapeuta que trate la dermatilomanía: los directorios de la TLC Foundation y la IOCDF, tu médico, y qué preguntar.
- [Cómo hablar de la dermatilomanía con tu familia y amigos | Gentleskin](https://gentleskin.app/es/guias/hablar-con-tu-familia/): Cómo contarle a tu familia o a tus amigos que te pellizcas la piel, y qué pedirles que hagan (y que no hagan).
